GENERAL BUSINESS

1.  Avalon City Council Policies Manual Review
  The Avalon City Council Policies Manual serves as a resource for Council Members,
  Department Heads, City Staff and members of the public in determining the manner in
  which matters of the City business is conducted. As a part of best its best practices, the
  City intended to review the manual each election cycle.
  Recommended Action
  Review the Avalon City Council Poilcies Manual, including proposed amendments and
  provide any input on revisions.

3.  Warrants
  Expenditures Submitted for Approval
  o Warrants from the General Fund in the amount of $842,983.29
  o Two payrolls totaling $566,563.53.
  o Four electronic fund transfers totaling $1,155,789.96.
  Recommended Action
  Approve total expenditures for July 8, 2024 through July 26, 2024 totaling $2,565,336.78.

4.  Fiscal Year 2023-2024 Fourth Quarter Treasurer’s Report
  State and Municipal Codes require the Treasurer to submit within 30 days following each
  fiscal quarter a report summarizing the City’s cash and investment balances. Attached is
  the Fourth Quarter Treasurer’s Report for FY23-24.
  Recommended Action
  Adopt the resolution accepting the FY23-24 Fourth Quarter Treasurer’s Report.

5.  Declare Surplus Equipment
  Historically, the City Council is presented with a list of items that are surplus, the Council
  formally declares the items as surplus, and then the declared items are sold via Public
  Surplus, donated to charity, or disposed of properly.
  Recommended Action
  Adopt a resolution declaring equipment listed in the resolution as surplus property and
  authorize the City Manager to dispose of it in accordance with City policy.

6.  Buffalo Nickel Transportation Permit Renewal
  According to the Avalon Municipal Code, initial Transportation Permits are valid for a
  period of three years and may be renewed for subsequent three-year periods. Buffalo
  Nickel’s renewal request includes a change in pick-up/drop-off location to the passenger
  loading zone at 107 Pebbly Beach Road (originally in front of the Trailhead).
  Recommended Action
  Approve the renewal of a Transportation Permit for Buffalo Nickel with stated conditions.

GENERAL BUSINESS (CONTINUED)

7.  Contract Award to Olyns, Inc. for Reverse Vending Machine
  City of Avalon is committed to enhancing its waste diversion and recycling efforts to
  promote sustainability and environmental stewardship. To support these goals, City staff
  issued a Request for Proposal (RFP) for the procurement of a reverse vending machine.
  The RFP process included issuing a public notice, receiving proposals, and evaluating
  them through a panel review and presentation process.
  Recommended Action
  Award a contract to Olyns Inc. for procurement of (1) reverse vending machine (RVM),
  including software, maintenance, and advertising services, in an amount not-to-exceed
  $35,000; and, authorize the City Manager to execute the contract and any related
  documents.

8.  Island Enterprises, Inc. Transportation Permit Application
  On July 10, 2024 Island Enterprises, Inc. (DBA Catalina Adventure Tours) submitted a
  Transportation Permit application and fee to the City to provide interior tours with pick
  up/drop-off at the Cabrillo Mole Ferry Terminal. Tours will follow the “Inside Adventure
  Tour” route shown in the map submitted (currently conducted by the 2006 Econoline Van).
  Recommended Action
  1. Receive presentation. 2. Discuss. 3. If consensus is met, approve the Transportation
  Permit for Island Enterprises, Inc. to utilize a commercial vehicle permit to conduct tours
  in an oversized vehicle with stated conditions.

9.  Contract Award to Public Sector Personnel Consultants for Total Compensation Study
  The City last completed a compensation study in 2015 as part of an overall classification
  survey and compensation study. Council approved funding for a market study to be
  completed in FY24/25. On April 16, 2024, Council authorized City staff to publish a
  request for proposal seeking consultation services to conduct a “Classification and
  Compensation Study”.
  Recommended Action
  Award a contract to Public Sector Personnel Consultants to complete a Total
  Compensation Study and provide on-call consulting services, in an amount not-to-exceed
  $45,000; and, authorize the City Manager to execute the contract and any related
  documents.

10.  Crescent Hillside Stabilization Contractor Procurement
  In 2023, a landslide began to develop below the Crescent Avenue Stairway.
  Approximately 100 cubic yards of earthen material below the wall rotated and slipped
  approximately six feet in elevation. In May 2023 the City Council declared a state of
  emergency and authorized the City Manager to negotiate and award a construction
  contract for a not to exceed $300,000 to stabilize the hillside.
  Recommended Action
  1. Make a finding that emergency measures must continue to be implemented to protect
  from economic loss of both City property and the adjoining private property, as well as
  reduce the hazardous conditions from a landslide below the Crescent Avenue Stairway.
  2. Authorize the City Manager or his designee to negotiate additional work to repair the
  Crescent Avenue Hillside/Stairway for a not to exceed $600,000. 3. Amend the FY 2024-
  25 Budget by increasing account 10550-6547, CIP Project #205002, by $358,977 for a
  total project sum of $875,000.

11.  Medical Cannabis Delivery Service Business Permit Termination and Revocation Appeal
  and New Application Solicitation
  In 2018 the City Council adopted a resolution of intent to award its first Medical Cannabis
  Delivery Business Service Permit to CJMH Group, Inc. dba Catalina Connect.
  Recommended Action
  1. Affirm, the City Manager’s decision to terminate a permit to provide medical cannabis
  delivery business services from CJMH Group Inc. dba Catalina Connect. 2. Authorize the
  entity, CJMH Group, mc, and/or owners, Steven Brereton or Carl Johnson to apply for a
  future City of Avalon Medical Cannabis Delivery Business permit without prejudice.

  3. Authorize the City Manager to refund an appeal fee submitted on behalf of Carl
  Johnson regarding the revocation of CJMH Group, Inc.’s permit. 4. Authorize City Staff to
  open the application process for a new medical cannabis delivery business permit holder.

12.  Extension of Moratorium on the Issuance of Transient Rental Licenses for Transient
  Rental Use to New Applicants
  On August 1, 2023, the City Council voted unanimously to establish, by urgency
  ordinance, a moratorium on the issuance of any new Transient Rental Licenses not filed
  prior to August 1, 2023. The City Council wishes to consider further regulation, consistent
  with its adopted LCP and General Plan, on how to properly and fairly address any
  proliferation of transient rentals within the City while recognizing the significant need for
  the public to have recreational access to the coast.
  Recommended Action
  Approve by four-fifths City Council vote an ordinance extending the moratorium on the
  issuance of Transient Rental Licenses for transient rental use to new applicants to July
  30, 2025.

SUBJECT:  Avalon City Council Policies Manual Review

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Review the Avalon City Council Policies Manual, including
proposed amendments and provide any input on revisions.

REPORT SUMMARY: In 2014, at the request of a City Council Member, City Staff developed
a policies manual to serve as a reference for Council Members regarding duties and
responsibilities of elected and appointed officials of the City of Avalon.

The Avalon City Council Policies Manual serves as a resource for Council Members,
Department Heads, City Staff and members of the public in determining the manner in which
matters of the City business is conducted.

As a part of best its best practices, the City intended to review the manual each election cycle.
However, due in part to timing of the 2020 General Municipal Election and the COVID-19
pandemic, the manual has not been reviewed or updated by City Council since 2018.

The ultimate goal of this process is to understand the guidelines of appropriate operating
procedures and policies.

GOAL ALIGNMENT: Not applicable.

FISCAL IMPACTS: None.

CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FOLLOWING RECOMMENDED ACTION: The Avalon City
Council and community may not be familiar with the City Council operating procedures and
policies.

FOLLOW UP ACTION: None.

ADVERTISING, NOTICE AND PUBLIC CONTACT:  This item was properly listed on the
posted agenda pursuant to the Brown Act.

 1.1  Intent

  1.1.1  It is the intent of the City Council of the City of Avalon to maintain a
  Policies Manual. Contained therein shall be a comprehensive listing
  of the Council’s current policies, being the rules and regulations
  enacted by the Council from time to time. The Policies Manual will
  serve as a resource for Council, staff and members of the public in
  determining the manner in which some matters of City business are
  to be conducted.

  1.1.2  This Policies Manual constitutes a compilation of current policies of
  the City and shall not be deemed to alter the effective date or
  application of such policies. Any policies newly adopted as a result
  of adoption of this Policies Manual shall be specifically identified as
  such by separate Council action prior to adoption of this Policies
  Manual.

1.2  Authority

  1.2.1  If any policy or portion of a policy contained within the Policies
  Manual is in conflict with State or Federal law, rules or regulations
  having authority over the City of Avalon, said State or Federal law,
  rules or regulations shall prevail.

 2.1  Basis of Authority

  2.1.1  The City Council is the unit of authority for establishing policy within
  the City. Apart from their normal function as a part of this unit, Council
  Members have no individual authority. As individuals, Council
  Members may not commit the City to any policy, act or expenditure.

  2.1.2  Council Members do not represent any fractional segment of the
  community within which the City is located, but are, rather, a part of
  the body, which represents and acts for the community as a whole.
  Council Members must act for the good of the entire community and
  not for their personal interests or agendas.

2.2  Attendance at Meetings

  2.2.1  Members of the City Council shall make every effort to attend all
  regular and special meetings of the Council unless there is good
  cause for absence.

  22.2  A vacancy shall occur if any member ceases to discharge the duty

  the results of the voting.

  3.9.3  Copies of minutes shall be made for distribution to and for approval

SUBJECT:  Fiscal Year 2023-2024 Fourth Quarter Treasurer’s Report

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Adopt the resolution accepting the FY23-24 Fourth Quarter
Treasurer’s Report.

REPORT SUMMARY: State and Municipal Codes require the Treasurer to submit within
30 days following each fiscal quarter a report summarizing the City’s cash and investment
balances. Attached is the Fourth Quarter Treasurer’s Report for FY23-24. The report was
shared with the City Treasurer prior to presentation to City Council.

The purpose of the report is to inform, on a quarterly basis, the City’s cash and investment
balances, the investment types, yields, and market values, and to ensure that the City’s
investments are in compliance with the City’s adopted investment policy. The report shows that
all of the City’s funds are in compliance with its investment policy. In general, operating cash is
held in US Bank checking accounts and any excess cash is invested in California’s Local
Agency Investment Fund (LAIF) and various certificates of deposit (CDs). In accordance with
Government Code sections 16429.1 and 53601 et seq., the City cannot invest more than 30%
of its portfolio in CDs. CDs accounted for 16.1% of the unrestricted cash and investments for
the quarter ended June 30, 2024.

On May 16, 2024, the City reinvested $5,207,200 in funds from maturing Treasury Bills into
new six month Treasury Bills with an estimated yield to maturity of 5.07%. The investment
should yield the City approximately $15,000 more than if the funds were held in LAIF over the
same period. The City also reinvested the three CDs that matured during the quarter into new
CDs maturing in 3-4 years with estimated yields between 4.43% 4.72%. The City takes a
  -

ladder approach with staggered maturities for its CD investments to balance its goals of high
rates in the short-term with stability to withstand market fluctuations in the longer-term. The
City will continue to assess for opportunities to increase its investment returns while
maintaining necessary liquidity and compliance with its investment policy.

The unrestricted cash balance for the fourth quarter of 2023-2024 totaled $26.1 million, an
increase of $2.9 million from the third quarter of 2023-2024. The unrestricted cash balance
includes cash from enterprise funds (e.g. Harbor, Sewer, Saltwater, and Solid Waste) not
available for general government functions. The increase in unrestricted cash is partially
attributable to the seasonality of visitor-driven tax revenues and the timing of significant capital
outlays anticipated to increase during the next fiscal year. While the majority of grant funding is
 performed on a cash reimbursement basis, the unrestricted cash and investments balance
also includes $2 million in grant pre-funding received in preparation for construction of the
second phase of the Cabrillo Mole Ferry Improvement project. The unrestricted cash balance
increased by $4.9 million compared to the fourth quarter of 2022-2023. The increase in
unrestricted cash balance from the prior fiscal year is attributable to visitor-driven tax revenues
exceeding budget estimates, the aforementioned grant-prefunding, and due to the timing of
significant capital outlays. The City expects to begin construction on several major capital
projects, including the second phase of the Cabrillo Mole Ferry Terminal rehabilitation and the
Five Corners Pedestrian Improvement project, during the fiscal year which will reduce future
unrestricted cash balances.

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Award a contract to Olyns Inc. for procurement of (1)
reverse vending machine (RVM), including software, maintenance, and advertising
services, in an amount not-to-exceed $35,000; and, authorize the City Manager to
execute the contract and any related documents.

BACKGROUND: The City of Avalon is committed to enhancing its waste diversion and
recycling efforts to promote sustainability and environmental stewardship. To support
these goals, City staff issued a Request for Proposal (REP) for the procurement of a
reverse vending machine. The RFP process included issuing a public notice, receiving
proposals, and evaluating them through a panel review and presentation process.

The REP was issued on July 5, 2024 inviting proposals for the supply and maintenance
of one reverse vending machine. The City received two proposals.

Based on the review and evaluation process, Olyns Inc. was selected as the preferred
vendor due to their comprehensive proposal, experience, and the technical capabilities
of the Olyns Cube RVM. Key features include:
  • Al-Based Identification: Accurate redemption of CRV deposits through Al-based
  container identification.
   • High-Capacity Storage: Proprietary crusher with high-capacity storage bins for
  plastic, aluminum, and glass, which allows for a smaller footprint.
  • User-Friendly Interface: Multilingual support and a user-friendly interface.
  • Real-Time Data: Real-time data transmission for monitoring and reporting.
  • Mobile Application: Olyns mobile application allows for CRV electronic pay outs
  via PayPal, customer support, competition among users, and detailed records.
  • Revenue Generation: The Olyns Cube include a 55” hi-definition video screen that
  can be used for advertisements, generating additional revenue to subsidize the
  costs of recycling and potentially expand RVM deployment.
  • Maintenance: Olyns to provide regular preventive maintenance, cleaning, and
  supplies to ensure optimal functionality. The Olyns application will allow for CR&R
  to be notified when the Cube is full, allowing for timely collection.
  • Timeline: The estimated implementation is for October 2024.

If approved, City staff will work with CR&R for the collection of recyclable materials from
the RVM, transport to the mainland for processing, and agreement with Olyns Inc. for
CRV funding transfer. In addition, City staff and CR&R will work on recycling center
regulatory approvals through CalRecyle.

Awarding the contract to Olyns Inc. for the procurement of one reverse vending
machine will enhance the City’s sustainability goals. If well received, additional RVMs
may then be implemented elsewhere. City staff recommend City Council approve the
contract award and authorize the City Manager to execute the necessary documents.

advertisement revenue will off-set annual maintenance fees. City staff will return to
Council with updates when known. Funding for this project has been allocated in the
current fiscal year’s budget under 13225-6547.

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

Dear Members of the Selection Committee,

We are pleased to submit our proposal for the procurement of one (1) Reverse Vending Machine (RVM)
for the City of Avalon. Our company, Olyns Inc (Olyns), is well-equipped to provide the required services,
including back-office software management, regular on-site maintenance, and the provision of
advertisement space on the machine.

Company Overview
Olyns is a Silicon Valley based technology company focusing on the implementation of a new paradigm
for recycling. Combining Al-enabled lOT hardware, innovative software and advertising demand, Olyns
enables our clients to save money, focus on core business and provide a highly desirable consumer
service while remaining in full compliance with all state and federal regulations. Our mission is to support
communities in their efforts to enhance sustainability and environmental stewardship.

Our RVM, the Olyns Cube, is used by some of the most popular grocery chains in California including
Safeways, Albertsons, Smart & Final, FoodMaxx, Lucky and many others. Outside of California, we
have installations with the Oregon Beverage Recycling Cooperative, at the State Capital in Georgia and
we were asked to install 2 Cubes at the White House during the annual Easter Egg Roll. Our deep
partnerships with Coca Cola and Pepsi Cola are expanding the Olyns Cube network to recycling deserts
in Texas and Georgia.

Project Understanding

The City of Avalon, situated on Catalina Island, requires an RVM to facilitate CRV redemption for plastic,
glass, and aluminum beverage containers. This initiative aligns with Avalon’s commitment to
sustainability and environmental protection. With a permanent population of approximately 3,500 and
over one million annual visitors, the RVM will serve both residents and tourists, contributing to the City’s
recycling goals and waste management efficiency.

Catalina Adventure Tours) submitted a Transportation Permit application and fee to the City of
Avalon to provide interior tours with pick-up/drop-off at the Cabrillo Mole Ferry Terminal. Tours

by the 2006 Econoline Van).

the interior of the island with the 2024 GMS Ram 3500. The vehicle capacity seats a total of
25, with 22 passenger seats, and is awaiting a commercial vehicle permit hearing with the
Vehicle Hearing Officer on Friday, August 23, 2024.

After meeting with the applicant, applicant has agreed to remove the 1984 American General
M809 from Santa Catalina Island in favor of the 2024 GMS Ram 3500 (already purchased and
on island). Island Enterprises, Inc. is offering to remove the existing 1984 American General by
January 2025 to allow existing City booked tours to conclude before removal. Vehicles are
over 200” and considered oversized per the Avalon Municipal Code.

SUBJECT:  Contract Award to Public Sector Personnel Consultants for
  Total Compensation Study

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Award a contract to Public Sector Personnel Consultants
to complete a Total Compensation Study and provide on-call consulting services, in an
amount not-to-exceed $45,000; and, authorize the City Manager to execute the contract
and any related documents.

REPORT SUMMARY: The City of Avalon last completed a compensation study in 2015
as part of an overall classification survey and compensation study. In the years
subsequent to the 2015 class/comp study, the Administration, with Council approval, has
modified the classification plan by establishing additional position descriptions and
compensation for new and existing classifications.

Administration requested and Council approved funding for a market study to be
completed in FY24/25. On April 16, 2024, Council authorized City staff to publish a
request for proposal (RFP) seeking consultation services to conduct a “Classification and
Compensation Study”. Although captioned as a class/comp study the scope of services
for the RFP specifically focused on a compensation analysis by requesting prospective
firms to “conduct a salary survey of comparison agencies, collect comparison agency
data, conduct a total compensation analysis to provide the City with an accurate
assessment of how its compensation plan compares with selected labor market agencies,
and finally analyze, review, and summarize data for presentation to the City.”

On May 13, 2024 the RFP was issued, inviting proposals to qualified human resource
consultants with the City receiving a total of eighteen. A selection panel reviewed the
proposals based on experience, approach, and cost. Four consultants (Reward Strategy,
AJG Gallagher, RGS, and Public Sector Personnel Consultants) completed virtual
presentations on July 29, 2024.

  Ranking  Vendor  Proposal
  1  Public Sector Personnel Consultant  $37,500
  2  AJG Gallagher
  —  $51,000
  3  Reward Strategy Group  $30,800
  4  Regional Government Services  $43,300
 It should be noted that because the title to the RFP referenced classification and
compensation study a handful of applicants also provided a cost of services to conduct a
classification study in addition to the compensation study. Those combined proposals
would more than double the cost set forth in the above proposals.

Based on the review and evaluation process, Public Sector Personnel Consultants was
selected as the preferred firm due to their comprehensive proposal, applicable local
government experience, inclusive approach, detailed presentation, twelve months of
support, and cost. City staff called references who confirmed positive work product. Public
Sector Personnel Consultants have also agreed to provide on-call consulting services at
a rate of $150 per hour for any additional consulting work to review any identified
classifications as needed through December 31, 2025. Therefore, staff is requesting a
total contract amount not to exceed $45,000.

The estimated completion date is expected by January 2025. This will allow adequate
time for staff, Council, and bargaining groups to review the reports and negotiate.

It should be noted the change in title terminology of a classification and compensation
study, to a focus on total compensation study is semantics. The scope of work in the REP
did not change and all proposals received included the total compensation study pursuant
to the published scope of services. Additionally, the City Manager has determined that
the outside compensation study contemplated herein in addition to the internal overall
review of the existing and amended classification plan is consistent with the “Maintenance
Cycle” outlined in the City’s Personnel Rules and Regulations (Chapter Six: Classification;
Section 4.2).

FISCAL IMPACTS: Funding of $50,000 has been allocated in the current year’s budget
under 10135-5005 to hire a consultant to complete the survey. An updated Total
Compensation Study will assist the City in determining competitive, fair and equitable
wages for all City employees.

GOAL ALIGNMENT: Fiscal and organizational stability.

CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FOLLOWING RECOMMENDED ACTION: The City may
not meet stated objectives in employee bargaining group MOU5.

FOLLOW UP ACTION: Execute a contract with Public Sector Personnel Consultants.

posted agenda pursuant to the Brown Act.

SUBJECT:  Crescent Hillside Stabilization Contractor Procurement

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): (1) Make a finding that emergency measures must continue to
be implemented to protect from economic loss of both City property and the adjoining private
property, as well as reduce the hazardous conditions from a landslide below the Crescent
Avenue Stairway. (2) Authorize the City Manager or his designee to negotiate additional work
to repair the Crescent Avenue Hillside/Stairway for a not to exceed $600,000. (3) Amend the
FY 2024-25 Budget by increasing account 10550-6547, CIP Project #205002, by $358,977 for
a total project sum of $875,000.

REPORT SUMMARY: On March 1, 2023, Governor Gavin Newsom proclaimed a state of
emergency in 13 California Counties due to winter storm conditions. In 2023, due to a series of
natural phenomena called “Atmospheric Rivers,” the City received an unprecedented amount
of precipitation and an increased number of wind events.

The weather conditions led to flooding, infrastructure failures, increase rock falls and mud
slides, the appearance of sink holes along the roadways, and damage to City parks and
facilities.

On March 21, 2023, the City Council adopted Resolution No. 23-07 making the appropriate
findings and declaring a Local State of Emergency due to the damages from the severe rain
and winds.

The resolution included an initial assessment of damage to City infrastructure, Exhibit A.

Of specific concern, a landslide began to develop below the Crescent Avenue Stairway, at a
location above the Catalina Island Yacht Club. Approximately 100 cubic yards of earthen
material below the wall rotated and slipped approximately six feet in elevation. Since the initial
event, anytime a significant rain event occurred additional material slipped downward in a slow
progression, with the amount of material movement relative to the amount and intensity of the
rainfall.

Staff consulted with the City’s on-call engineering consultants and determined that the material
needs to be removed, but the wall that provides the foundation for the stairway was still
competent; however, with additional rain, additional earthen material slipped and exposed the
 lower wall embedment. Staff again consulted with its on-call consultant, and the contractor
that originally constructed the wall. It was determined that a corrective action needed to be
pursued to protect the integrity of the wall.

On March 21, 2023, the City Council voted unanimously to:
  1. Make a finding that emergency measures must be implemented to protect from
  economic loss of both City property and the adjoining private property, as well as
  reduce the hazardous conditions from a landslide below the Crescent Avenue Stairway.
  2. Make a finding that due to the need to respond with a highly qualified contractor relative
  to the work scope that public bidding is inefficient with this specific work scope and
  should be dispensed with.
  3. Authorize the City Manager or his designee to negotiate and award a construction
  contract for a not to exceed $300,000 to complete the work.

Since the adoption of the Emergency Declaration Resolution and authorization to negotiate
and award a contract City Staff, under the direction of the Director of Emergency Services, has
worked to identify an apporopriate contractor to mitigate storm damages throughout Avalon,
including the damage at Crescent Avenue Hillside.

Unfortunately, due to the limited footprint to work from both at the bottom of the hillside and
  —

the top as well as the steep incline. Staff had an extremely difficult time engaging a qualified
  —

contractor to perform any scope of work.

Additionally, the Atmospheric River conditions of 2023 were experienced throughout the State
causing significant storm damage in much of California. The increased need for qualified
contractors in other regions futher inhibit the City’s ability to identify and engage an appropriate
vendor to perform the necessary mitigation work.

As a temporary measure, in late 2023 City Staff installed a tarp to mitigate further erosion in
the area.

In April 2024, City Staff became aware of a contractor with the availability and ability to perform
the necessary work to stabilize the hillside. The City received an initial proposal from Arizona
Drilling & Blasting on May 1, 2024. The proposal includes a preliminary defined scope of work
estimated at $282,000; however, due to general complications of the project, the contractor
recommended, and City Staff have agreed, for work to be performed on a time and material
basis (T&M). On May 3, 2024 the City entered into an agreement with Arizona Drilling &
Blasting to perform the necessary scope of work on a T&M basis for a not to exceed sum of
$300,000.

The project began on May 5, 2024. Arizona Drilling & Blasting and other vendors have worked
to provide project mobilization of personnel and equipment to the island and up the hillside to
the limited access project site, excavated an area to perform the work, drilled and placed 17
tieback anchors to depths of 40 feet into bedrock anchorage, installed 17 walers (horizontal
steel beams) to transfer wall loads to tieback anchors, drilled and installed eight underdrains to
depths of 20 feet into the hillside, manufactured and installed 30 concrete laggings (horizontal
 beams) to retain the wall backfill where the slipout exposed unrestrained soil, installed an
underdrainage system over and down the hillside to direct excess subterrain drainage to the
road below, and restored the hillside area with an engineered backfill I erosion control.

Due to the complexity of the scope, difficulty associated with the location and the discovery of
various concealed conditions, the project budget has expanded.

City Staff recommend the City Council authorize the City Manager, or his designee, to
negotiate additional work to repair the Crescent Avenue Hillside/Stairway for a not to exceed
$600,000. Revising the sum has been discussed with the contractor and the new sum should
be sufficient for the remaining scope of work.

If approved, Staff recommend the City Council authorize an amendment to the FY 2024-25
Budget by increasing account 10550-6547, CIP Project #205002, by $358,977 for a total
project sum of $875,000. This sum includes monies needed in addition to the construction
contract including services of a geotechnical engineer, crane services, barge services,
materials, lodging for the project worker due to the unforeseen conditions.

City Staff and the contractor anticipate this project to be completed by mid-August 2024.

  MEDICAL CANNABIS DELIVERY OPERATING PLAN

A Medical Cannabis Delivery Operating Plan (Operating Plan”) is required for all medical
cannabis delivery businesses in the City of Avalon (City”). The Operating Plan must address
and meet, at a minimum, the requirements as set forth in Avalon Municipal Code (“AMC”) Title 5
Chapter 20. Any statements made in the Operating Plan may not supersede any local and/or
state laws, rules, and regulations.

Each section of the Operating Plan should be clearly labeled with a cover sheet for each
section. The Operating Plan must have page numbers in the bottom right hand corner. DO NOT
staple or bind the Operating Plan. You may submit the Medical Cannabis Delivery Service
Business Application (“Application”) and the Operating Plan in a three ring binder or in an
envelope. Both the Application and the Operating Plan must be submitted at the same time.

I. General Description of Services

Each applicant should submit an Operating Plan generally describing their proposed business
model. You must identify whether you will be distributing your own products, another businesses
products, or both. The Operating Plan should provide an account of the proposed day-to-day
operations of the facility, including a description of each step in the delivery process
(transportation, storage, quality assurance, packaging, labeling, etc.) that the medical cannabis
delivery business will engage in, and where each step will occur in the facility. Plans should also
provide a general description of the types of medical cannabis products that will be distributed
from the facility.

II. Security

Applicants should provide a detailed description of their security plans. The security component
should be broken down into operational and facility security categories. Appropriate plans will
have considered all potential security threats and planned for any contingency needed for these
situations. A successful applicant will have both written and physical mechanisms in place to
deal with each specific situation. A detailed schematic diagram of alarm systems and security
camera placements that also details when all security measures will be operational should be
provided.

  a. Operational Security

Applicants will detail their operational security including but not limited to general security
policies for the facility, employee specific policies, training, sample written policies, transactional
security, confidential information security, and third- party contractor security. This includes
storing all finished medical cannabis products in a secured and locked room, safe, or vault, and
establishing limited access areas accessible only to authorized personnel. The security plan
should include measures to prevent the diversion of medical cannabis to persons under the age
of 18. The security plan should also consider measures to prevent individuals from remaining on
the premises if they are not engaging in activity expressly related to the operations of the
business, and ensure that medical cannabis is not inhaled, smoked, eaten, ingested or
 otherwise consumed on the property, or in the parking areas of the medical cannabis delivery
business property.

This list is not intended to fully capture all areas for applicant consideration but to guide
applicants into considering all possible security concerns related to the operation of a medical
cannabis delivery facility. The applicant should give consideration to every possible scenario
and provide a response to those scenarios.

  b. Facility Security

Applicants must review and address Section 5-20.100(B) of the AMC as part of their Operating
Plan. Further, applicants should provide a description of the overall facility security. In
particular, the applicant should address ingress and egress access, perimeter security, product
security (at all hours), internal security measures for access (area specific), types of security
systems, and security personnel that will be employed.

The security plan should describe the enclosed, locked facility (incorporated into the building
structure, or securely attached thereto) that will be used to secure or store medical cannabis
and cash when the location is both open and closed for business. The security plan should also
detail the steps taken to ensure medical cannabis is not visible to the public. The facility security
plan should also discuss the fire and burglar alarm systems. The security plan should identify
the company monitoring the alarm, and provide confirmation that the security company is
staffed twenty-four (24) hours a day, seven (7) days a week.

Each medical cannabis delivery business shall install and maintain a fully operational digital
video surveillance and camera recording system. The medical cannabis delivery facility security
plan should further describe the digital video surveillance and camera recording system that will
be used to monitor the front and rear of the property, all public right-of-ways and any parking
lots under control of the medical cannabis delivery business, all points of ingress and egress at
the medical cannabis delivery business, all points of sale within the medical cannabis delivery
business, all areas within the medical cannabis delivery business where medical cannabis
products are to be prepared for delivery, and all limited access areas within the medical
cannabis delivery facility.

The video and surveillance system shall, at a minimum, meet the following requirements:
  • Capture a full view of the public right-of-ways and any parking lot under the control of the
  medical cannabis business;
  • Provide HD quality, color rendition and resolution to allow the ready identification of any
  individual committing a crime anywhere on or adjacent to the exterior of the medical
  cannabis delivery business property;
  • Record and maintain video for a minimum of forty-five (45) days. Video surveillance and
  recording records shall be held in confidence by all employees and for legitimate law
  enforcement activity to resolve criminal activity;
  • Medical cannabis delivery businesses are responsible for ensuring that all video or
  surveillance equipment is properly functioning and maintained, so that playback quality
  is suitable for viewing and the equipment is capturing the identity of all individuals and
  activities in the monitored areas;
  • The system shall be capable of recording all monitored areas in any lighting conditions
  and must be housed in a designated, locked, and secured room or other enclosure with
  access limited to authorized employees. Medical cannabis delivery businesses must
   keep a current list of all authorized employees and service personnel who have access
  to the surveillance system and/or room on the permitted premises;
  •  A sign shall be posted in a conspicuous place near each monitored location on the
  interior or exterior of the premises, stating “All Activities Monitored by Video Camera” or
  “These Premises are Being Digitally Recorded”, or otherwise advising all persons
  entering the premises that a video surveillance and camera recording system is in
  operation at the facility and recording all activity; and
  •  All exterior camera views must be continuously recorded 24 hours a day and all interior
  cameras views shall be recorded during all hours that the facility is open for business.

In addition to the standards set forth above, the applicant must include in their security plan,
compliance with Section 5-20.100(B) of the AMC and state law regulations concerning the
same. Any security measures that exceed these standards are highly desirable.

III. Transportation

Applicants should describe the methods that will be used to transport medical cannabis
products to and from other medical cannabis businesses. In addition, applicants should detail
the security precautions that will be taken to prevent theft or diversion of medical cannabis
during transport. This may include securing cannabis products in a locked box affixed to the
vehicle, securing the vehicle when unattended, installing alarm systems, motion detectors, or
panic buttons within the vehicle, and taking other necessary steps to protect the driver(s) and
cannabis products. The applicant must describe how they will comply the provisions set forth in
Section 5-20.110 of the AMC and state regulations concerning delivery/transportation services.

IV. Product Storage & Tracking

The Operating Plan should describe the methods that will be used to properly store and
segregate different batches of medical cannabis goods within the delivery facility. This includes
a plan to control temperature and humidity, avoid exposure of medical cannabis products to
direct sunlight, and prevent the entry of environmental contaminants such as smoke and dust.
The Operating Plan should also identify how medical cannabis will be tracked and monitored to
prevent diversion and theft. The Operating Plan should describe how the delivery business will
maintain records of all medical cannabis products, including the level of detail cannabis
inventory will be tracked (e.g. origin of shipment, date of transfer, total weight, expiration/sell-by
date, etc.). In addition to the foregoing, the applicant must describe how it will comply with state
regulations concerning product storage and tracking.

The Operating Plan should provide a description of the point of sale software that the medical
cannabis delivery business will utilize to track inventory and sales of medical cannabis, and the
internal procedures the medical cannabis delivery business will follow for cash handling and
audits.

V. Laboratory Testing & Disposal of Contaminated Products

Applicants should also discuss how the medical cannabis delivery business will ensure proper
sampling and testing of medical cannabis products prior to receiving a shipment to the medical
cannabis delivery business. The Operating Plan should describe the steps that the delivery
facility will take when notified from a testing agency that the tested medical cannabis does not
meet appropriate health standards. Briefly describe how the medical cannabis delivery business
will ensure that rejected medical cannabis is not released to the public. The Operating Plan
 should also describe the methods that will be used to make medical cannabis waste unusable
and unrecognizable, and where medical cannabis waste will be stored prior to removal from the
medical cannabis delivery business.

In addition, the Operating Plan should describe how the medical cannabis delivery business will
transport medical cannabis waste from the medical cannabis delivery business facility site to a
solid waste facility or landfill.

VI. Product Complaints

Applicants should describe policies for receiving, recording and handling product complaints
associated with the use of medical cannabis provided by the delivery facility. Policies should
include:
  • A process for accepting product complaints at the delivery facility;
  • Identification of data elements to record a complaint (e.g. name of individual submitting
  complaint, identity of product used, description of events, etc.)
  • Review of product complaints from appropriate staff;
  • Procedure for determining the proper response, which may include contacting the
  cultivator/manufacturer supplying the product, contacting dispensaries receiving the
  product, notifying public health authorities; and/or
  • A process for determining any other additional follow-up that may be needed.
  • A process for notifying appropriate City staff of complaints received by the medical
  cannabis delivery business.

VII. Odor Control

Applicants should provide a description of what methods will be used to ensure that odor
generated inside the medical cannabis delivery business facility is not detected outside the
medical cannabis delivery business property. This should include a description of the odor-
absorbing ventilation and exhaust system, and how that system will prevent odor from leaving
the medical cannabis delivery business property. The Operating Plan may also describe
alternative methods to control odors, such as a carbon filtration or other system. The applicant
must also describe how it will comply with the odor control regulations outlined in Section 5-
20.090(B) of the AMC and state laws regulating the same.

VIII. Toxic Material Control

Applicants should provide a description of any toxic, flammable, or other materials that will be
used or kept at the medical cannabis delivery business, the location of such materials, and how
such materials will be stored. This should include all materials regulated by a federal, State, or
local government that would have authority over the medical cannabis delivery business if it was
not a medical cannabis delivery business. Applicants should also describe methods used to
comply with limitations on discharge into the wastewater system of the City, as set forth in the
AMC.

IX. Community Involvement

Applicants should provide a detailed description of their plans to participate in community
service within the City. These plans may include, but are not limited to, involvement with non
profit associations, neighborhood associations, and community groups. Applicants should
 demonstrate how they intend to provide their local community with community benefits and
mitigate any nuisance and/or negative impacts that the medical cannabis delivery business
facility’s existence may cause.

Applicants should show how they plan to have minimal nuisance or negative impacts on their
neighbors and community. Nuisance/negative impacts include but are not limited to: noise, odor,
increased foot or vehicle traffic, increase in waste or water production, impacts to right of way
access, and/or increase in safety related concerns. Applicants should detail how they will
revitalize the building/site, provide neighborhood improvements, and will be a beneficial/positive
neighbor to the neighborhood. Applicants must also provide the name, telephone number and
email address of a community relations contact as required under Section 5.20-120 of the AMC.

X. Fire Plan

Applicants should provide a detailed description of their fire prevention, suppression, alarm and
life safety systems. A fire inspection will be required annually to assure the City that adequate
fire safety measures remain in place. An appropriate plan will have considered all possible fire,
hazardous material, and inhalation issues/threats and will have both written and physical
mechanisms in place to deal with each specific situation. A detailed description of the fire
prevention, suppression, alarm and life safety systems that also includes when all fire
prevention measures will be submitted for approval and be operational should be required.

XI. Employee Safety

Applicants should provide a summary of the safety protocols that will be adopted by the delivery
facility, including, but not limited to: staff training, protective equipment, hazardous material
handling, emergency communication/response, etc. Businesses must conform to all Cal OSHA
workplace safety standards, specifically Title 8 of the California Code of Regulations. Applicants
should describe the policies and procedures used by the business to help prevent
contamination of any medical cannabis product. This may include hand washing, employee
training, use of facemasks/gloves, prohibiting employees who are showing signs of illness, open
wounds, sores or skin infections from handling cannabis, etc. The applicant must also aver that
its employees have read and understand all of the City’s cannabis regulations prior to
commencing operations.

(c)  At the hearing the appellant may present any information they deem relevant to the decision appealed.

(d)  At the conclusion of the hearing, the City Council may affirm, reverse or modify the decision appealed.

SUBJECT:  Extension of Moratorium on the Issuance of Transient Rental
  Licenses for Transient Rental Use to New Applicants

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Approve by four-fifths City Council vote an ordinance
extending the moratorium on the issuance of Transient Rental Licenses for transient rental use
to new applicants to July 30, 2025.

REPORT SUMMARY: On August 1, 2023, the City Council voted unanimously to establish, by
urgency ordinance, a moratorium on the issuance of any new Transient Rental Licenses not
filed prior to August 1, 2023 for a 45 day period (Urgency Ordinance No. U-1212-23). The
ordinance was adopted in response to numerous concerns from property owners and residents
regarding visitors utilizing property for which a Conditional Use Permit or Transient Rental
License has been issued allowing for transient use. Additionally, evidence locally and
nationally supports the concerns that the proliferation of short term rentals in residential
neighborhoods may contribute to increases in housing costs, reduction of housing stock,
overall street congestion, excessive noise, traffic hazards, inability to access parking,
additional strain on City services and certain property crimes within the City. Further,
community members have raised their experiences with these issues in public comment at
various meetings of the City Council and Planning Commission and other stakeholder
meetings, as described further in this report. Increases in housing cost and reduction of
housing stock are particularly important issues to the City of Avalon community given that it is
not possible to travel to Catalina Island by vehicular means from other areas in Los Angeles
County and commuters mostly travel to the Island by ferry. That has historically acted as a
deterrent to individuals in Los Angeles County from accepting work in the City due to the
increased cost and time necessary to travel to the City from the mainland. Consequently,
increases in housing costs and limits on the housing supply then reduce available supply of
labor on the Island.  V

On September 15, 2023, the City Council adopted by a vote of 4 ayes, 1 absent (Mayor
Marshall) Urgency Ordinance No. U-1213-23 extending the moratorium for an additional 10
months and fifteen days. This additional time was needed to further determine the level of
impact on the City of Avalon and to propose and establish common sense regulations to
protect the health, safety and welfare of the community.

In response to public health and safety concerns, as well as to study whether there is a
correlation between a real or perceived proliferation of Conditional Use Permits and Transient

 Rental Licenses and available housing stock, including affordable housing for full-time Avalon
residents and employees of Avalon businesses, City Council requested Staff to perform an
analysis of the current Conditional Use Permits and Transient Rental Licenses.

Since the establishment of the moratorium, City Staff has conducted the following activities
specifically related to the moratorium:

  -  Held a stakeholder meeting on Tuesday, September 22 at 6 p.m. approximately 4 community
  members attended in person, with approximately 20 attending virtually. Meeting discussion
  included quality of life issues, specifically noise, trash, and other community impacts associated
  with transient rentals.

  -  Held a stakeholder meeting on Wednesday, September 30 at 6 p.m. approximately 20
  community members attended in person, with approximately 40 attending virtually. Meeting
  discussion included financial benefits and impacts, sustainability and housing impacts
  associated with transient rentals.

  -  Staff compiled an extensive list of comments and regulatory options from community members
  both in attendance at the meetings as well as those who provided written comments directly to
  Staff. Attached to this memo is a compilation of comments received.

  -  From October 1, 2023 to December 1, 2023, the City conducted a survey to determine the
  overall impact of Conditional Use Permits and Transient Rental Licenses amongst Island
  visitors, residents and property owners. The survey also provided insight into participant’s
  thoughts regarding potential enhanced regulations and/or additional enforcement.

  -  Survey results were presented to the Planning Commission on February 21, 2024 and are
  attached to this report for reference.

  -  In Spring 2024, the City contracted with iWorks to assist in the development of a comprehensive
  database to assist in the management and tracking of the City’s Conditional Use Permits and
  Transient Rental Licenses. As City staff complete the analysis of the current Conditional Use
  Permit and Transient Rental License holders, the database is updated to include these
  individuals/addresses.

A previous analysis conducted in March 2023 of the City’s business license database as well
as transient rental license records indicated they were approximately 378 Conditional Use
Permit and 33 Transient Rental License holders in Avalon total of 411 short term rental units.
  —

This number is not consistent with the number of known and active short term rental units
reporting to the City. On March 1, 2024, City staff began the task of culling through more than
40 years of historical records detailing the issuance, transfer and revocation of Conditional Use
Permits and Transient Rental Licenses in order to make a final determination of the number of
Conditional Use Permits and Transient Rental Licenses issued and active within the City of
Avalon. This analysis has been painstakingly slow but is necessary in order to establish a
comprehensive list of every property located in the City that has the ability to operate as a
short term rental unit. To date, staff has completed approximately 80 percent of this review
process.

65059.00002\42530304. I
 The City Council wishes to consider further regulation, consistent with its adopted LCP and
General Plan, on how to properly and fairly address any proliferation of transient rentals within
the City while recognizing the obligation to balance the needs of long term housing.

The foundation of any decision to regulate short term rentals is the number and location of
every existing unit. Without this clear determination, Council cannot fairly and adequately
identify the common sense regulations required to not only protect existing housing stock but
also protect the interests of the business community. As more analysis is needed, an
extension of the moratorium will allow issues associated with determining the overall number
of Conditional Use Permits and Transient Rental Licenses, and their impact on public health,
safety and welfare, as well as their impact upon affordable long—term housing and city
revenues to be further vetted.

Staff recommends that the City Council approve by four-fifths City Council vote an ordinance
extending the moratorium on the issuance of Transient Rental Licenses for transient rental use
to new applicants to July 30, 2025.

 Section 2.  Purpose. The purpose of this urgency ordinance is to extend the
  moratorium on the issuance of any new Transient Rental Licenses for
  transient rental use for the statutorily authorized period, until such time as
  the Avalon City Council can study the issue, and develop, clarify or amend
  Code requirements and standards as it relates to transient rental use and its

  immediately necessary for the preservation of the peace, health and safety

  further public peace, health, and safety risk in that an over
  abundance of Transient Rental Licenses for transient rental use may
  be responsible for street congestion, excessive noise resulting in loss
